slides.headline: Tailbone sore every time you sit?
slides.sub: Common, often slow to settle, and very manageable.

slides.title: What it usually is
slides.body: Tailbone pain, or coccydynia, often follows a fall onto the bottom, long stretches of sitting, or childbirth. Sometimes there's no clear trigger at all, and that's common too.

slides.title: Take the pressure off
slides.body: Try a wedge or U-shaped cushion with a cut-out at the back. Lean forward slightly when you sit so your weight goes through your sit bones instead of your tailbone.

slides.title: Stand up more often
slides.body: Pain often builds the longer you sit and spikes as you stand. Short, frequent breaks and a standing option for calls or reading can make the day much easier.

slides.title: Ease the muscles around it
slides.body: Tension in the pelvic floor and glutes can add to tailbone pain. Relaxed breathing, gentle stretches and soft glute work often help. A physio can guide what suits you.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: Pain after a significant fall, pain that keeps getting worse, fevers, numbness, or changes to bladder or bowel control should be checked by your GP promptly.

slides.headline: Make sitting easier again
slides.body: Our Sydney CBD and Chatswood physios assess what's driving the pain and give you practical ways to sit, move and settle it. Book online — link in bio.

caption:
Wincing every time you sit down? Tailbone pain is more common than people think.

It often follows a fall onto the bottom, long hours of sitting, or childbirth, and sometimes it just appears. It can be slow to settle, but most people do improve with a few practical changes.

A wedge or cut-out cushion, leaning slightly forward, standing up more often and easing tension in the surrounding muscles are a good starting point. Pain after a significant fall, fevers, numbness or bladder and bowel changes should be checked by your GP.

story.headline: Sore tailbone when you sit?
story.body: Try a cut-out cushion, lean slightly forward and stand up every 20 to 30 minutes.
